A. Santa Monica Realignment Plan – The One-Year Mark
Recommended Action
Staff recommends that the City Council review the progress made during the first year of the Santa Monica Realignment Plan , provide direction on the revitalization initiatives outlined in this report, and approve the following actions to continue implementation of the Plan:
1. Adopt a finding of no possibility of significant effect pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines, and findings of categorical exemption pur suant to Section 15273 (Rates, Tolls, Fares, and Charges) and Section 15324 (Regulations of Working Conditions);
2. Adopt a Resolution of the City Council of the City of Santa Monica establishing new classifications and adopting salary rates for various listed positions (Attachment A);
3. Approve certain Building and Safety Division position and classification changes to effectuate actions approved by Council at its July 28, 2026 meeting (Attachment B);
4. Adopt a Resolution of the City Council of the City of San ta Monica updating certain user fees (Attachment C);
5. Authorize the City Manager to negotiate and execute an agreement with 3Di Systems, Inc. for rent registry software and administrative services for the Housing and Human Services Department for an initial term of two years, which is a recommended award being made as an exception to the competitive bidding process pursuant to the City's Procurement Policy;
6. Adopt a Resolution of the City Council of the City of Santa Monica establishing a standalone Propert y Registration Certificate Fee (Attachment D);
7. Approve the Downtown Catalyst Incentive Program Guidelines (Attachment E), and authorize staff to implement the new economic development program;
8. Authorize staff to implement the Downtown parking pilot programs with Metropolis, Inc. related to Downtown parking structure optimization, implementing a Downtown valet parking program, and implementing the proposed Zoox license agreement as described in this report; and
9. Approve changes to the FY 2025-26 and FY 202 6-27 Revised Budgets, as described in the Financial Impacts & Budget Actions section of this report (requires 5 votes).
